items.prompt: For n<=20 and exponent k up to 10^18, what controls the number of matrix-power loop iterations?

options.text: The numeric value k, with one multiplication per unit.
options.why: Binary exponentiation handles bits instead of subtracting one repeatedly.

options.text: The primality test for M, which the function runs each time.
options.why: The function does not test primality; the task supplies M.

options.text: The bit length of k, at most 60 for the allowed positive k.
options.why: Each iteration halves k. Each product uses O(n^3) arithmetic operations.

options.text: Exactly n iterations, regardless of k.
options.why: Matrix dimension controls product work, not the number of exponent bits.

items.explanation: Each iteration halves k. Each product uses O(n^3) arithmetic operations.
